label: THE UNTOUCHABLE
voice_script: In the world of athletics, some records aren't just broken, they're obliterated into a different dimension. Usain Bolt's 9.58 second 100-meter dash in 2009 wasn't just a win; it was a redefinition of human speed. This wasn't just a world record; it was a chasm. Nobody, not even the sport's greatest, has come within a full tenth of a second of his time. For seventeen years, that impossible mark has stood firm, an enduring monument to human capability that simply refuses to fall. And science agrees. Expert models, scrutinizing every variable, now project this monumental achievement will remain untouched, not being surpassed until at least the 2060s. What's even more astonishing? He stepped onto the track for his signature event and simply never lost, retiring with a perfect, undefeated record. Usain Bolt: a phenomenon whose legend grows with every passing year, forever cemented as the fastest man to ever live.
